summary:
Li–Zhang state the local GSpin arithmetic Siegel–Weil identity Int^ε(L)=∂Den^ε(L) for F=Q_p, p odd, m=n+1≥3, and its good-prime semi-global consequence over Q. The proof separates horizontal cycles from vertical Deligne–Lusztig contributions, compares density and geometric recurrences on a quadratic plane, and then uses p-adic uniformization.

Independent review: revise; this extraction is partial. Original 45 bundles leave definitions and key intermediate results unsplit. Added pinned-library providers and explicit K/Chow/cycle-map inputs do not close the whole dependency graph. Finite-field count boundaries, Corollary3.6.2, full-type-overlattice helpers, distribution extension, higher Chern-character signs and component-preserving isometries must not be copied uncorrected. A Tate-class comparison is not a K-class equality.

Routes1–2 remain unaccepted candidate briefs. Routes3–5 have appropriate owners as bounded source contributions, not certified proofs. Generic local/global quadratic classification is imported from existing Tau Ceti roadmaps; local density extensions belong in GN.3, the isotropic-plane theta/distribution calculation in MP.3, and Tate's p-divisible-group theorem in R07.1. Foundational K-theory, cycle maps, Fourier theory and canonical Shimura models are imports, not fresh GSpin constructions.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.1 = Theorem 4.15.1 (local arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula for GSpin Rapoport–Zink spaces)
items.statement: Let F = Q_p, p odd, m = n + 1 ≥ 3, ε ∈ {±1}, N = N^ε_n the connected GSpin Rapoport–Zink space attached to the self-dual lattice H^ε_m, and V = V^ε_m its space of special quasi-endomorphisms (χ(V) = ε, Hasse invariant −1). For every O_F-lattice L ⊆ V of rank n: Int^ε(L) = ∂Den^ε(L), where Int^ε(L) = χ(N, O_{Z(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(x_n)}) (1.2.0.1) and ∂Den^ε(L) = −(d/dX)|_{X=1}Den^ε(X, L), Den^ε(p^{−k}, L) = Den(H^ε_{m+2k}, L)/Den(H^ε_{m+2k}, H^ε_n), with Den^ε(X, L) = −X^{val(L)}Den^ε(1/X, L).
items.locator: §1.2, (1.2.0.1), Theorem 1.2.1, pp.2–4; Theorem 4.15.1, p.31; proof §9.3, pp.65–67, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: The orthogonal analogue of the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture; m = 4 was known (Gross–Keating/Wedhorn for ε = +1, Terstiege for ε = −1). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.

items.name: Theorem 1.3.1 = Theorem 12.9.1 (semi-global arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula)
items.statement: For F = Q, V of signature (n − 1, 2) with m = n + 1 ≥ 3, p > 2 with K_p = GSpin(Λ_p) hyperspecial, V the incoherent positive definite nearby space, ϕ_K ∈ S(V^n_f) p-admissible (K-invariant, ϕ_{K,p} = 1_{(Λ_p)^n}) and T ∈ Sym_n(Q)_{>0}: Int_{T,p}(ϕ_K)q^T = c_K·∂Eis_{T,p}(z, ϕ_K), with q^T = ψ_∞(½ tr Tz) = e^{πi tr Tz} and c_K = (−1)^n/vol(K). Proof: p-adic uniformization reduces Int_{T,p} to Theorem 4.15.1 and Remark 3.4.9, the prime-to-p orbital integrals give Π_{v≠p,∞} W_{T,v}(1, 0, ϕ_{K,v}) [Kud97b, Prop. 1.2], and q^T = c_∞W_{T,∞} [BY21, Prop. 4.3(ii)]; the sign is γ^n_V = (−1)^n.
items.locator: Theorem 1.3.1, p.5; Theorem 12.9.1 and proof, pp.76–77, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: Remark 1.3.2: a global version (all T, all places) is harder for GSpin than for unitary groups (no split places, p = 2). Remark 1.3.3: F = Q_p is needed for [HP17, Kim18a]. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 (local density of integral representations)
items.statement: For nondegenerate quadratic O_F-lattices M,L of ranks m,n, Rep_{M,L}(R) is the functor of quadratic-form-preserving R-linear maps L⊗R→M⊗R. The local representation density is the stabilized normalized congruence count of Definition3.1.1. If the generic representation scheme is nonempty, its dimension is n(2m−n−1)/2; retain that nonemptiness condition when using this exponent. The empty case and existence of the density limit must be handled separately.
items.locator: Definition 3.1.1, (3.1.1.1)–(3.1.1.2), p.10, authors' final version (2 March 2022)

items.name: §3.4 (odd corank): normalized local Siegel series, weight polynomials, Theorems 3.4.5–3.4.6, Corollary 3.4.7, Remarks 3.4.8–3.4.9
items.statement: Nor^ε(X, L) = (1 − sgn(H^ε_{n+1})q^{−(n+1)/2}X)Π_{1≤i<(n+1)/2}(1 − q^{−2i}X²) and Den^ε(X, L) ∈ Z[X] with Den^ε(q^{−k}, L) = Den(H^ε_{n+1+2k}, L)/Den(H^ε_{n+1+2k}, H^ε_n); weight polynomials m(t, s; X) = (1 + s q^{(t−1)/2}X)Π_{0≤i<(t−1)/2}(1 − q^{2i}X²), m^ε(t, s; X) = m(t, s; εX), weight factors m^ε(t, s) = −(d/dX)m^ε|_{X=1}. Theorem 3.4.5: Den^ε(X, L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} X^{2ℓ(L′/L)}m^ε(t(L′), sgn_{n+1}(L′); X) (generalizing [CY20, Cor. 3.16]). Theorem 3.4.6 (Ikeda): Den^ε(X, L) = w^ε(L)X^{val(L)}Den^ε(1/X, L), w^ε(L) = (det L, −(−1)^{C(n+1,2)}u)_Fϵ(L_F) ([Ike17, Thm. 4.1(2)] for n odd and ε = +1; the same proof works in general). Corollary 3.4.7: if w^ε(L) = −1, ∂Den^ε(L) = Σ_{L′} m^ε(t(L′), sgn_{n+1}(L′)). Remark 3.4.8: ∂Den^ε(L^♭ ⊥ M) = ∂Den^{ε′}(L^♭) for M self-dual. Remark 3.4.9: W_T(1, k, 1_{Λ^n}) = Den(Λ ⊥ H^+_{2k}, L) [Kud97b, Prop. A.6], so W′_T(1, 0, ϕ_0) = ∂Den^ε(L)·Nor^ε(1, L)·log q (3.4.9.2). At t=0 the weight polynomial is separately 1. The chosen unit u has χ(u)=ε. Self-dual cancellation changes ε to the discriminant sign of the complementary ambient space.

items.name: Theorem 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.2 (induction formula for the local Siegel series)
items.statement: Let L^♭ be an integral rank n−1 lattice with last fundamental invariant a_{n−1}, let x⊥L^♭ have val(x)>a_{n−1}, and put L=L^♭⊥⟨x⟩ and L̃=L^♭⊥⟨ϖ^−1x⟩. items.name: Lemma 9.3.1 (reducing L^♭)
items.statement: For integral L^♭ of rank n − 1 with invariants (a_1, …, a_{n−1}) and x ∈ Ω(L^♭): (i) if x ∉ L^♭ ⊥ W^{≥a_{n−1}}, then L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ with val(L′^♭) < val(L^♭) (Smith normal form of the fundamental matrix); (ii) if x ∈ L^♭ ⊥ W^{=a_{n−1}} and L^♭ is co-isotropic, then L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ with L′^♭ co-anisotropic and val(L′^♭) = val(L^♭).

items.name: Étale tensors, special endomorphisms and Lemma 5.5.2 (§§5.4–5.5)
items.statement: For a formally smooth base, a crystalline Tate tensor has a unique integral étale Tate tensor matching it under the crystalline comparison [Kim18a, Thm. 7.1.6]; applied to π_crys this gives π_ét with image V_ét, and for z ∈ N(O_K) a self-dual lattice V_ét,z̄ ≅ V inside End(T_pX). SEnd°(X) = {f : i_K(f) ∈ V_F} = {f : i_κ̄(f) ∈ V} (Definition 5.5.1), SEnd(X) = SEnd°(X) ∩ End(X); Lemma 5.5.2: SEnd(X) = i_K^{−1}(V) (via Tate's theorem); Corollary 5.5.3: z ∈ Z(M)(O_K) iff M ⊆ i_κ̄(i_K^{−1}(V)), giving an embedding M → V of quadratic modules.

items.name: Definition 4.6.1 and Proposition 4.10.1 (special cycles Z(L); special divisors are flat Cartier divisors)
items.statement: Z(L) ⊆ N is cut out by ρ_univ ∘ x ∘ ρ_univ^{−1} ∈ End(X_univ) for x ∈ L; it depends on the O_F-span and is nonempty only for integral spans. items.name: Deligne–Lusztig varieties Y_W, minuscule cycles V(Λ) and the Bruhat–Tits stratification (§§4.7–4.9)
items.statement: For the non-split quadratic space W of dimension 2(d + 1) over F_q, Y_W is a connected component of the locus in OGr_{d+1}(W) with dim(U + σ(U)) = d + 2, smooth projective of dimension d, stratified by generalized Deligne–Lusztig varieties X_{P_i}(w_i) with open stratum of Coxeter type [HP14, Prop. 3.8; HLZ19, Prop. 2.5.1] (Y_W ≅ P¹ for d = 1). For a vertex lattice Λ ⊆ V, t(Λ) is even with 2 ≤ t(Λ) ≤ t_max = m − 2, m − 1, m for (m even, ε = +1), m odd, (m even, ε = −1) (4.8.0.1) [HP17, 5.1.2], and V(Λ) = Z(Λ) (reduced [LZ18, Thm. B]) ≅ Y_{W_Λ,κ̄}, W_Λ = Λ^∨/Λ. N^red = ⋃ V(Λ), V(Λ) ⊆ V(Λ′) iff Λ ⊇ Λ′, V(Λ) ∩ V(Λ′) = V(Λ + Λ′) or ∅, strata V(Λ)° ≅ Y°_{W_Λ} [HP17, §6.5, Thm. D(iii)], and Z(L)^red = ⋃_{L ⊆ Λ} V(Λ) (4.9.0.2) [Soy17, Prop. 4.2].

items.name: Quasi-canonical and Gross–Keating cycles, horizontal cycles and Theorem 5.3.1 (§§5.1–5.3, 5.6)

items.name: Proposition 6.1.1, Remark 6.1.2 and Definition 6.2.1 (the vertical part lives on N^red)
items.statement: For L^♭ of rank n − 1, Z(L^♭)_V is supported on N^red: a formal curve through a unique closed point would specialize a non-basic isocrystal to a basic one, but its (L^♭_F)^⊥-component lies in B(T) for the torus T = SO(W), where specialization is trivial [RR96, §1.7, Thm. 3.6]. Hence Gr^{n−1}K^{Z(L^♭)}_0 = Gr^{n−1}K^{Z(L^♭)_H}_0 ⊕ Gr^{n−1}K^{Z(L^♭)_V}_0 (6.2.0.1) and ^𝕃Z(L^♭) = Z(L^♭)_H + ^𝕃Z(L^♭)_V canonically (6.2.1.1). The torus argument also reproves [LZ, Lemma 5.1.1] (Remark 6.1.2).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.1 and Theorem 6.3.2 (the Tate conjecture for the Deligne–Lusztig varieties Y_d)
items.statement: For Y_d = Y_W (dim W = 2(d + 1), non-split) with strata X°_i and closures X_i: for every s≥1, the Frobenius power F^s, with F=F_{q²}, acts semisimply on H^{2j}(Y°_d)(j), H^{2j}(X°_i)(j), H^{2j}(Y_d − X_i)(j) with no invariants for j ≥ 1 ([Lus76, 7.3 case ²D_n, 6.1]); hence H^{2i}(Y_d)(i)^{F^s=1} is spanned by the classes of the irreducible components of X_{d−i} (the Tate conjecture holds for Y_d) and equals the generalized 1-eigenspace (as [LZ, Thm. 5.3.2]). Here 0≤i≤d and coefficients are Q_ℓ, ℓ≠p; the Tate statement concerns the 1-generalized eigenspace, not all odd cohomology.

items.name: Theorem 7.4.1, Lemma 7.4.2, Remarks 7.4.3–7.4.4 and Corollaries 7.4.5–7.4.6 (intersections with Deligne–Lusztig curves)

In the co-anisotropic case the finite sum has a unique Schwartz extension (Corollary7.4.6, qualified by E9). items.name: Definition 9.2.1, Lemma 9.2.2 and Proposition 9.2.3 (recurrences for the geometric partial Fourier transform)
items.statement: Int^⊥_{L^♭,V} ∈ L¹_loc(W^an) (in S(W) if L^♭ is co-anisotropic) lies in D(W)_k for some k: it is O(W)(F)-invariant (Remark 4.11.5 and Theorem 7.2.2), O_F^×-invariant, supported in W^{≥−k}, and its Fourier transform γ_V Int_{L^♭,V}|_W is supported on W° (Corollary 7.5.3). Hence (i) for co-anisotropic L^♭ it is constant on W° (translation invariance by (W°)^∨ ⊇ W°), and (ii) for co-isotropic L^♭, Int^⊥(x) − Int^⊥(ϖ^{−1}x) is constant on W°° ∩ W^an (Corollary 9.1.4).

items.name: Theorem 9.3.2 (Int_{L^♭} = ∂Den_{L^♭} on Ω(L^♭)) and the proof of Theorem 4.15.1
items.statement: For L^♭ of rank n − 1, Int_{L^♭} = ∂Den_{L^♭} on Ω(L^♭). Proof: non-integral L^♭ gives 0 = 0; a_1 = 0 reduces to smaller n by the cancellation laws (4.14.0.4), (3.4.8.1); otherwise induct on val(L^♭): by Lemma 9.3.1 the difference is 1_{L^♭} ⊗ φ^⊥ with supp φ^⊥ ⊆ W^{≥a_{n−1}} (co-anisotropic) or W^{≥a_{n−1}+1} (co-isotropic, using the co-anisotropic case); the partial Fourier transforms of the vertical parts agree near W^{=−1} ∪ W^{=0} (∪ W^{=1}), and the recurrences of Propositions 8.1.2 and 9.2.3 propagate the vanishing. Theorem 4.15.1 follows by writing L = L^♭ + ⟨x⟩.
items.locator: Theorem 9.3.2 and proof, pp.66–67, authors' final version (2 March 2022)

items.name: Incoherent quadratic spaces over A (§10)
items.statement: Paper-specific coherent/incoherent adelic quadratic data of rank m=n+1≥3 over a totally real field: a global discriminant class, local Hasse signs of finite support, χ_V((a_v))=Π_v(a_v,disc(V_v)), and total sign ε(V). Import admissible-invariant realization (64), including real signatures, to define coherence and nearby spaces. Total positive definiteness means signature(m,0), not(n,0). The nearby space at the distinguished real place has signature(m−2,2); at a finite place change its Hasse sign and retain all other local forms.
items.locator: §10, p.68, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: Generic local/global classification is imported from64, not constructed in GSpin heights. The residual incoherent-data/Weil-section adapter needs one automorphic owner; route1 remains rejected. E12 records the signature typo.

items.name: The Weil representation ω_{χ,ψ} of G_n(A) × O(V) (§11.3)
items.statement: On S(V^n): ω(m(a))ϕ(x) = χ(m(a))|det a|^{m/2}ϕ(x·a), ω(n(b))ϕ(x) = ψ(tr ½T(x)b)ϕ(x), ω(w_n)ϕ = γ^n_V ϕ̂, ω(h)ϕ(x) = ϕ(h^{−1}x), ω(1, t) = t for n even, with the Weil constant γ_V = γ(det V, ψ)^{−1}γ(ψ)^{−m}ϵ(V) [Kud97b, p.642]; G_n(A) = Sp(W)(A) for n odd and the metaplectic Mp(W_A) (global Rao cocycle, canonical splittings over Sp(W)(F) and N(A)) for n even.
items.locator: §§11.1, 11.3, pp.68–70, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: MP.4 plans the adelic metaplectic cover and the global Weil representation.

items.name: Siegel Eisenstein series, Whittaker factorization and incoherent Eisenstein series (§§11.1–11.4)
items.statement: I_n(s, χ) = Ind_{P_n(A)}^{G_n(A)}(χ·|·|^{s+(n+1)/2}) with χ extended to M_n(A) via the Weil index for n even; E(g, s, Φ) = Σ_{P(F)\Sp(W)(F)} Φ(γg, s) with meromorphic continuation; E_T = Π_v W_{T,v} for nonsingular T with W_{T,v}(g, s, Φ_v) = ∫ Φ_v(w_n^{−1}n(b)g, s)ψ(−tr ½Tb)dn(b) and E′_T = Σ_v E′_{T,v} ((11.2.0.2)–(11.2.0.3)); the standard Siegel–Weil section Φ_ϕ(g) = ω(g)ϕ(0); for incoherent V the central value vanishes and ∂Eis, ∂Eis_T, ∂Eis_{T,v} are defined; W_{T,v}(g, 0, ϕ_v) ≠ 0 only if v ∉ Diff(T, V) [Kud97b, Props. 1.3–1.4], so ∂Eis_{T,v} ≠ 0 only if Diff(T, V) = {v} (Remark 11.3.1); the classical E(z, s, ϕ) on H_n with Gaussian ϕ_∞(x) = e^{−π tr T(x)} and its Fourier expansion (11.4.0.2).
items.locator: §11, (11.2.0.2)–(11.4.0.2), Remark 11.3.1, pp.68–71, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: Split this bundle by owner: MP.5–MP.6 own genuine automorphic spaces and coherent/incoherent sections; AS.2 supplies linear-group continuation, with a proved cover adapter needed for even n. The GSpin arithmetic identity is a consumer; route1 is rejected.

items.name: The semi-global arithmetic intersection number Int_{T,p}(ϕ_K) (§12.8)
items.statement: For T ∈ Sym_n(F)_{>0} with diagonal t_1, …, t_n and special ϕ_K: Int_{T,p}(ϕ_K) = χ(Z(T, ϕ_K), O_{Z(t_1,ϕ_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(t_n,ϕ_n)})·log p (12.8.0.3), extended C-linearly.

items.name: Definition 9.1.1, Lemma 9.1.2, Proposition 9.1.3 and Corollary 9.1.4 (invariant distributions on an isotropic plane)
items.statement: For a 2-dimensional quadratic space W over F (odd residue characteristic), D(W)_k consists of distributions that are O(W)(F)- and O_F^×-invariant, supported in W^{≥−k}, with Fourier transform supported in W°. K_0(ϖ^k) = N^−(ϖ^kO_F)A(O_F)N(O_F) for k ≥ 1 (Lemma 9.1.2). If W is isotropic: dim D(W)_k = 2k for k ≥ 1, via the Weil representation of SL₂, D(W)_k = D(W)^{O(W)(F) × K_0(ϖ^k)^t}, the isomorphism S(W)_{O(W)(F)} ≅ I(1) of [Kud97b, Prop. 1.1] and newforms for SL₂ [LR07, Prop. 3.2.4]; an explicit basis φ_0 (val(x) + 1 on W°), φ_1 = 1_{W^{≥−1}} and φ_{2i−2}, φ_{2i−1} (i ≥ 2, split by the square class of ϖ^i(x, x)), realized as O(W)-orbital integrals (Proposition 9.1.3); every T ∈ D(W)_k is represented by φ with φ(x) − φ(ϖ^{−1}x) constant on W°° ∩ W^an (Corollary 9.1.4). At k=0 the basis is φ_0 alone and the dimension is1. The displayed functions are regular distributions, not arbitrary extensions across the cone.
items.locator: §9.1, Definition 9.1.1, Lemma 9.1.2, Proposition 9.1.3, Corollary 9.1.4, pp.61–64, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: The count 2k agrees with the double cosets B(F)\SL₂(F)/K_0(ϖ^k) (two A(O_F)-orbits for each intermediate cusp). Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 as a source. Import explicit Weil operators from MP.2; MP.3 owns the orthogonal coinvariant and distribution specialization. The SL₂ principal-series newform dimension remains a separately source-qualified input, not classical GL₂ newforms. E12 corrects the representative ϕ_1 sign without changing its support.

items.name: Tate's theorem for p-divisible groups over O_K
items.statement: For F=Q_p and K/F̆ finite as in§5.4, the Tate module functor on p-divisible groups over O_K is fully faithful: Hom_{O_K}(X,Y)≅Hom_{Z_p[Γ_K]}(T_pX,T_pY), in particular an endomorphism-ring isomorphism. This is the Tate theorem invoked in Lemma5.5.2, not finite-flat generic-fibre uniqueness with a small-ramification bound.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.5.2, p.36, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: R07.1 is the p-divisible/Tate-module owner. Its separately planned Raynaud theorem has e<p−1; do not impose that bound on Tate or delete it from Raynaud. The original Tate paper is still a source-acquisition dependency, not freshly read in full here.

items.name: Clifford algebra, vector map and universal property
items.statement: For a quadratic form Q on an R-module over a commutative ring, CliffordAlgebra Q is the tensor-algebra quotient by v²=Q(v). Its linear vector map squares to Q and has the universal property for linear maps into R-algebras satisfying that relation.
items.note: Read Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Basic.lean:74,114,122,139 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Use the paper's normalization Q(v)=(v,v); no unnoticed factor of2. Integral GSpin, grading/tensors and Kuga–Satake constructions are separate.

items.name: Discriminant and signed discriminant of a regular form class
items.statement: Over a field with2 invertible, the plain discriminant is the square class of the product of diagonal weights; the signed discriminant adds rank.choose2 times the class of−1 in the additively written square-class group. Discriminants of orthogonal sums multiply.
items.locator: §2.1, published pp.1360–1362
items.note: Read TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/RegularFormClass/Discriminant.lean:95,114,157 at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. This does not supply the local Hasse symbol or O_F-lattice classification.

items.name: Witt extension on regular subspaces
items.statement: An isometry between regular subspaces of a finite-dimensional quadratic space over a field with2 invertible extends to an isometry of the whole space. The declaration requires nondegeneracy of the restricted source form, not a lattice or spinor-norm condition.
items.locator: Used in Remark4.11.5, published p.1392
items.note: Read TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Witt/Extension.lean:45 at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Obtaining determinant1 by reflection on a nondegenerate complementary line is an adapter; forcing trivial spinor norm is not a consequence (E3).

items.name: Field-valued orthogonal and special-orthogonal spinor norms
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional nondegenerate form over a field with2 invertible, the Clifford norm descends to O(Q) modulo squares, and restriction gives a homomorphism on SO(Q).
items.locator: §4.4–4.5 and Remark4.11.5, published pp.1385–1386,1392
items.note: Read TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/SpinorNorm/Basic.lean:143,213 at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Reflection convention is class(−Q(v)); on an even product the extra minus signs cancel. An integral GSpin similitude is not this square-class carrier.

items.name: Image of Spin equals the spinor-norm kernel
items.statement: Under the field, finite-dimensionality, invertibility-of2 and nondegeneracy hypotheses, range(Spin(Q)→SO(Q))=ker(spinorNorm).
items.locator: Proof input needed by Remark4.11.5, published p.1392
items.note: Read Spin/SpinorNorm/Basic.lean:323 at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. This is not surjectivity onto all rational SO-points. The p-unit-similitude subgroup has an additional valuation condition.

items.name: Fourier integral for a bilinear pairing and additive character
items.statement: Given a bilinear pairing L:V×W→k, a circle-valued additive character e, a measure μ and a complex normed-space-valued function f, VectorFourier.fourierIntegral is ∫v e(−L(v,w))f(v)dμ. The paper's plus convention uses e=ψ^−1 or the negative pairing.
items.locator: §2.2, published pp.1362–1363

items.name: Derived category of an abelian category
items.statement: Given an abelian category and its universe-qualified localization choice, DerivedCategory is cochain complexes localized at quasi-isomorphisms, with the localization functor Q.
items.note: Read Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Basic.lean:87,95 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. This is the ordinary category, not the formal-scheme support K-group, derived tensor, perfectness or Euler characteristic required here.

items.name: Algebraic cycles on a scheme
items.statement: An algebraic cycle with coefficients in a zero-bearing type is a coefficient function on scheme points with locally finite support.
items.locator: §12.2 and§12.5, published pp.1451–1454

items.statement: Construct K_Z(X) from perfect complexes acyclic off Z, its localization/excision/change-of-support maps and products. Dévissage requires the regularity/resolution conditions actually used; do not identify K_Z(X) with K(Z) unconditionally.

items.statement: For smooth finite-type schemes over a perfect field and prime-to-characteristic coefficients, construct cycle classes with rational-equivalence invariance, proper-pushforward and intersection/cup-product compatibility, Gysin maps and the projection formula.

items.name: K-valued intersection function of a stratum
items.statement: For x≠0, define K_{V(Λ)}(x) in K̄⁰(V(Λ)) as the image of the derived intersection V(Λ)∩^LZ(x) under the support-K/dévissage map and quotient in(7.6.0.2). Use the actual complex class [O]−[O(−Z(x))], not its negative.

items.name: K-theoretic local modularity
items.statement: Let Λ have type2d+2≥4. For every Q-linear l:K̄⁰(V(Λ))→Q, l∘K_{V(Λ)}, initially on V\{0}, extends uniquely to a Schwartz–Bruhat function on V and satisfies Fourier(l∘K_{V(Λ)})=γ_V(l∘K_{V(Λ)}), γ_V=−1. The uniqueness is within the Schwartz class, not arbitrary distributions.

items.name: Higher local modularity of the intersection function
items.statement: For a vertex lattice Λ of type2d+2≥4, the intersection function Int_{V(Λ)} has a unique Schwartz–Bruhat extension and Fourier(Int_{V(Λ)})=γ_V Int_{V(Λ)}, γ_V=−1.

items.name: Local quadratic classification and Hilbert/Hasse invariants

Preserve the rank1 Hasse−1 and rank2 discriminant−1/Hasse−1 exclusions; translate to the signed discriminant convention used here.

items.name: Global admissible invariants and quadratic-form realization
items.statement: Over a number field, regular positive-rank forms correspond to admissible systems with a global discriminant, specified real signatures, locally realizable Hasse signs of finite support and total product1. The real signatures are part of the invariant, not recoverable from Hasse signs alone.
